candidates.description: Summarizes canonical i32 additive recurrences, including degree-two iteration polynomials, with exact modulo-2^32 arithmetic.

legality_obligations.description: Require the supported canonical loop and induction shape.
Prove the state update through the shared SCEV affine recurrence model.
Derive an exact iteration count before replacing the loop.
Preserve zero and negative-iteration behavior.
Preserve i32 modulo-2^32 arithmetic, including polynomial division ordering.
Reject loop bodies with unsupported side effects.
Prove every observable loop live-out is reconstructed exactly.
Apply only when the closed form is expected to reduce work.

candidates.description: Replaces proven closed small-domain pure i32 transitions with bounded binary-lifting jump tables.

legality_obligations.description: Require a small compile-time constant state domain.
Exhaustively prove that every domain state transitions within the domain.
Require a deterministic transition without memory, calls, or floating-point effects.
Prove the signed iteration domain and preserve short or non-positive loops.
Use an injective bounded state and jump-table encoding.
Interpret every transition with exact i32 arithmetic.
Enforce per-table and whole-pass storage and code-size limits.
Apply only above the frozen trip-count profitability threshold.

candidates.display_name: Strict same-domain loop fusion and temporary contraction
candidates.description: Fuses adjacent canonical loops with identical domains while preserving dependence order and contracting proven temporary storage.

legality_obligations.description: Require adjacent canonical single-latch loops.
Prove both loops traverse the same iteration domain.
Reject cross-iteration flow, anti, or output dependences that fusion would reorder.
Require proven pointer roots and mod/ref behavior.
Preserve the order of all supported observable effects.
Contract temporary storage only after proving its complete lifetime and non-escape.
Reject first-loop header or body state observed by the second loop or later code.
Apply only when fusion or temporary contraction is expected to reduce work.

candidates.description: Accelerates small-dimensional pure i32 affine state transitions with exact modulo-2^32 binary lifting.

legality_obligations.description: Require a fixed one-to-three-dimensional state vector.
Prove simultaneous state updates form one affine transition.
Derive the exact signed remaining trip count.
Preserve zero and negative-iteration behavior.
Perform matrix lifting with exact i32 modulo-2^32 arithmetic.
Reject floating-point and unsupported modulo-sensitive operations.
Reject memory, call, and other unsupported body effects.
Prove every state live-out is reconstructed exactly.
Retain the original loop for unprofitable short executions.

candidates.description: Memoizes reachable states of bounded two-dimensional pure ranked recurrences without dense-domain enumeration.

legality_obligations.description: Require direct finite recursion with exactly two i32 state parameters.
Prove every recursive edge decreases a composite well-founded rank.
Reject memory, external calls, floating point, and other impure context.
Memoize only states reached by the original recursive control flow.
Prove the bounded two-dimensional memo key is injective.
Preserve original base-case and recursive evaluation order.
Preserve exact i32 recurrence arithmetic.
Enforce the frozen memo-domain and storage cap.
Preserve the public ABI and avoid external runtime dependencies.
Apply only to recurrences with demonstrated repeated reachable states.

candidates.display_name: Incremental prefix and suffix scan reuse
candidates.description: Reuses incremental prefix or suffix reductions across a canonical outer loop after alias, bounds, and side-effect proofs.

legality_obligations.description: Require a canonical repeated prefix or suffix domain.
Prove the incremental recurrence equals the original nested reduction.
Restrict reassociation to exact i32 addition semantics.
Prove source loads and output stores do not alias or escape.
Require a pure inner reduction kernel.
Preserve empty and one-element domains.
Prove all rewritten source and output indices remain in bounds.
Reject unsupported escaping inner-loop values.
Apply only when the incremental form reduces asymptotic work.
